clue.text: Reckless general's assistant involved in plan

indicators.note: something involved in another is wrapped up inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a map is a plan or chart
ADC is an aide-de-camp, an officer assisting a general

explanation.surface: A general's aide gets caught up in a rash scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A madcap person or scheme is wildly impulsive, the same as reckless.

clue.text: Fragrant festoon finally thrown out by a dreamer

indicators.note: a letter thrown out is ejected, so it is deleted from the word

parts.note: a romantic is an idealistic dreamer

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word festoon

explanation.surface: A sweet-smelling garland is discarded by an idealist.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of 'festoon', N, is removed from ROMANTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Aromatic means having a pleasant, pungent smell, so fragrant.

clue.text: It may prevent someone seeing a waterfall

definitions.meaning: an eye condition clouding the lens and blocking sight
a large, steep waterfall or torrent

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a clouding of the eye's lens that blocks vision and a great cascade of water.

clue.text: Burning obsession with extremely pretty country

indicators.note: taking a word extremely means using its extremes, its first and last letters

parts.note: Romania is a country in south-east Europe

explanation.surface: A consuming passion for a rather attractive nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pretty' reads as an adverb meaning rather, but it gives its first and last letters, P and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyromania is a compulsion to start fires, literally an obsession with burning.

clue.text: A fabulous beauty swallows it following an appetizer

indicators.note: one piece swallowing another takes it inside itself

parts.note: a peri is a beautiful fairy of Persian legend, a creature of fable
taken as written
F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale beauty gulps something down after a starter.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is a drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite, so it serves as an appetizer.

clue.text: Senior officer's broadcast on leading Roman poet, say

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: to air something is to broadcast it
chief means leading or principal

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: Martial was a Latin poet famed for his epigrams

explanation.surface: A top commander has been on the radio talking about an eminent classical poet.
explanation.walkthrough: MARTIAL, the Roman epigrammatist, is pronounced like MARSHAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Air chief marshal is a very senior rank in the Royal Air Force.

clue.text: Road workers dressed in right clothing

indicators.note: pieces dressed in another are clothed by it, so they go inside it

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, written here as AI
men can mean workers, as in management and men

explanation.surface: A gang of road menders is kitted out in the correct gear.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1, Britain's main north-south road, is read with the figure 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for clothing or garments.

clue.text: Army's obsessive enthusiasm for Pacific island

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve, and the 's adds an S
a mania is an obsessive enthusiasm

explanation.surface: Soldiers have a craze for a faraway island.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania is the island state south of mainland Australia, bordering the Pacific region.

clue.text: Paid to endorse useful response to inquiry

parts.note: fee'd means paid a fee
to back something is to endorse or support it

explanation.surface: Being paid to support a helpful answer to a query.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paid' is read as FEE'D, given a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Feedback is information returned in response, often as a helpful reaction to a request.

clue.text: King Harry is leading fiddler

indicators.note: the piece said to be leading comes first, in front of the other

parts.note: Harry Potter, the boy wizard of the novels
ER is Edward Rex, King Edward's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A monarch called Harry heads the band as its chief violinist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Harry' looks like one person, but they are two pieces, and Harry, the boy wizard's first name, gives his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A potterer idles about with trivial tasks, which is what a fiddler (one who fiddles about) does.

clue.text: He abandons the topic for a series of lies

indicators.note: a word that abandons another leaves it, so those letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written before the removal
taken as written, the letters to be removed
an issue is a topic under discussion

explanation.surface: A man drops the subject in favour of a pack of untruths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandons' signals the removal; 'He' looks like a person giving up the topic, but it is just the letters taken from 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tissue of lies is an idiom for an interwoven series of falsehoods.

clue.text: Show disapproval when member of orchestra swigs drink with husband

indicators.note: a container that swigs a drink takes it inside

parts.note: a harp is one of the instruments in an orchestra
rum is an alcoholic drink
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogies

explanation.surface: An orchestral player tuts while taking a swig with her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: To harrumph is to make a gruff throat-clearing sound expressing displeasure.

clue.text: Crudely paint bunk gold and black

parts.note: a bunk is a bed
AU is the chemical symbol for gold
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A decorator slaps gold and black on a bunk bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedaub is to smear or daub paint on something clumsily.

clue.text: Notices a bad sportsman

indicators.note: letters that are bad are spoilt or disordered, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Reviews call a certain athlete poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notices' reads as reviews, but with 'a' its letters are rearranged by 'bad'.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoeist is someone who paddles a canoe as a sport, hence a sportsman.

clue.text: Lingerer's unsteady progress across river and, later, lake

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: a later insertion is made after the first, also inside the word
a piece across another lies over it, enclosing it

parts.note: a stagger is an unsteady walk

explanation.surface: Someone dawdling lurches over a river and then a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into STAGGER first, then L is put in near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A straggler falls behind the rest, lingering at the back.

clue.text: Way to secure business levy, once

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast within, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
CO is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: A street plan is a means of guaranteeing a historic trade tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Scot was an old tax or levy, surviving in the phrase scot-free.

clue.text: Union leader left with counterfeit notes? It's scandalous!

parts.note: a sham is a counterfeit or fake
E and F are musical notes

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter

explanation.surface: A trade union boss caught with forged banknotes causes outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union leader' looks like a trade unionist, but it gives U; 'notes' are musical, not banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Shameful means disgraceful, deserving shame, as something scandalous is.

clue.text: Dutiful, providing sleeping-place for king in East

indicators.note: one piece standing for another replaces it

parts.note: the Orient is the East
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex
a bed is a place to sleep

explanation.surface: A loyal subject finds a bed for the monarch in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: BED replaces the R of ORIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Obedient means willing to obey, so dutiful.

clue.text: Liquor container clubs seek

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for the card suit clubs
to ask for something is to seek it

explanation.surface: Nightclubs go looking for a barrel of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A cask is a barrel for holding wine, beer or spirits.

clue.text: Stick around to put on good protective coat

indicators.note: one piece placed around another encloses it

parts.note: to cling is to stick fast
to add is to put something on top, as in adding to a total

explanation.surface: Glue something on to apply a sound protective layer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good' belongs to the definition, since cladding is a sound outer covering; 'around' puts one piece inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Cladding is a covering layer fixed to a building or pipe to protect it.

clue.text: One getting engaged starts to suffer parent's reprimand

indicators.note: starts of words are their first letters

parts.note: a rocket is British slang for a severe telling-off

explanation.surface: An engaged person begins to suffer a parent's scolding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting engaged' suggests betrothal, but a sprocket's teeth engage a chain; 'rocket' as a telling-off is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprocket is a toothed wheel whose teeth mesh with, or engage, a chain.

clue.text: Retiring party saw royal residence

indicators.note: a retiring piece draws back, so its letters run in reverse

parts.note: LAB is short for Labour, the political party
a saw is an old saying, and its moral is the lesson it teaches

explanation.surface: A party leaving office spotted a palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' is not the past tense of see but a proverb, here a moral.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral Castle in Scotland is a residence of the British royal family.

clue.text: Singer stabbed by gangster in New York port

indicators.note: something stabbed by another has it pushed into it

parts.note: a buffo is a singer of comic opera roles
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A vocalist was knifed by a mobster in a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Buffalo is a city and port on Lake Erie in New York State.

clue.text: Adapt fog disperser brought back in yacht

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, which contains it

parts.note: MY is the abbreviation for motor yacht

indicators.note: something brought back returns the way it came, so its letters are reversed

parts.note: FIDO was a wartime system for dispersing fog from airfields

explanation.surface: Change a fog-clearing machine shipped back aboard a pleasure boat.
explanation.walkthrough: FIDO (Fog Investigation and Dispersal Operation) cleared fog from RAF runways in the Second World War; 'brought back' makes ODIF.
explanation.definitionFit: To modify something is to alter or adapt it.

clue.text: Dance gear one of Lorna's family shortened

parts.note: rig means equipment or gear
A means one, as in a single thing

indicators.note: a shortened word loses its last letter

parts.note: Lorna Doone is the heroine of R. D. Blackmore's novel, so her family are the Doones

explanation.surface: A dance outfit belongs to someone from a famous fictional clan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' cuts the final E from DOONE to give DOON.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigadoon is a lively old dance for couples, of French origin.

clue.text: Reputation of retreating enemy

indicators.note: a retreating thing goes backwards, so the run of letters is reversed

parts.note: a name is a reputation, as in making a name for oneself
taken as written

explanation.surface: A foe in retreat loses standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns the whole run NAMEOF backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Foeman is an archaic word for an enemy in war.

clue.text: Capital invested in brothels in Kingston

indicators.note: something invested in a phrase is placed within it, so the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: Money has been sunk into some bordellos in a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money, matching 'invested', but it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital city of Finland.

clue.text: Cooked tortilla on the shore

indicators.note: cooked letters have been doctored, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Mexican flatbread is prepared at the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Littoral means relating to or situated on a coast or shore.

clue.text: Manipulate hot material very well

parts.note: to rig is to manipulate fraudulently, as in rigging an election

indicators.note: the word hot is treated as raw material to be worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Handle the scorching stuff with great skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very well' looks like an adverb for the handling, but it is the exclamation of agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Righto is an informal British exclamation of agreement, like OK or very well.
